hellohouse.title: Hello House
hellohouse.about_title: A Warm Space in the Heart of Kaohsiung
hellohouse.about_desc: Located in the heart of Yancheng, Kaohsiung, Hello House is your perfect base for exploring the harbor city. We specialize in private rental spaces for 8 to 26 guests. No strangers—just you and your loved ones enjoying the spacious island kitchen, sharing laughter in the living room.
hellohouse.feat1_desc: Open-plan space with IH stove, microwave, and full tableware. Perfect for group dining and hot pot parties.
hellohouse.feat2_desc: Mahjong table and 43-inch smart TV to keep the party going.
hellohouse.feat3_desc: From double to six-person rooms with flexible configurations. All rooms feature separate wet/dry bathrooms and Instagram-worthy hanging chairs.
hellohouse.rooms_sub: All 6 rooms feature pocket spring mattresses, separate wet/dry bathrooms, smart TV, and climate control
hellohouse.cta_bottom_sub: Whether it's a family reunion or a friends' party, we're ready for you.
hellohouse.meta_title: Hello House | Kaohsiung Private Villa | 8-26 Guests near Pier-2
hellohouse.meta_desc: Private group stay in Kaohsiung's Yancheng District. Hello House fits 8-26 guests with an island kitchen, manual mahjong table, multiple room types, and a walkable route to Pier-2 Art Center.

godin.title: Godin House
godin.hero_desc: Nestled in a quiet Yancheng alley, this five-story standalone building offers a warm private rental experience for 10 to 12 guests.
godin.about_desc: Godin House is the refined second property in the Hello Stay family. Enjoy the entire five-story building privately with no other guests. Designed in a cozy family style, every stay feels like coming home. Starting from NT$10,000 on weekdays—the best value for small group rentals.
godin.rooms_sub: Five-story standalone with 4 rooms, all with private bathrooms and climate control

godin.meta_desc: Five-story private villa in Kaohsiung's Yancheng district. Godin House accommodates 4-12 guests with four ensuite rooms, a cozy lounge, and simple prep space. Near Pier-2.

guide.meta_title: Kaohsiung Travel Guide to Pier-2, Yancheng & Private Stays
guide.meta_desc: Explore Kaohsiung Yancheng district! 20 mins by MRT from Zuoying High-Speed Rail Station, 10 mins walk to Pier-2 Art Center. Stay at Hello Stay premium private villa with island kitchen and mahjong.
guide.hero_sub: Pier-2 Art Center, Yancheng Food, and the Ultimate Private Villa Experience
guide.section1_desc: Hello Stay offers a 100% private villa rental with no other guests sharing your space. Cook together in our spacious island kitchen, play and chat around our manual mahjong table, or stream your favorite shows on our large Smart TV. It is the perfect choice for family reunions, group getaways, friend gatherings, or corporate retreats.
guide.section2_desc: Arrive easily from Kaohsiung International Airport (KHH) or Zuoying HSR Station via the MRT metro system. We are just a 5-minute walk from Yanchengpu Station (O2) Exit 4. No need to worry about the stress of foreign driving or renting a car. For guests arriving by car, we also provide detailed local parking information.
guide.section3_title: Art & Yancheng Street Food Within Walking Distance
guide.section3_desc: Walk just 10 minutes to reach Kaohsiung's iconic Pier-2 Art Center, the Great Harbor Bridge rotary show, and Dayi Warehouse cluster. Around the historical Yancheng neighborhood, taste traditional duck rice, legendary milk teas, and delicious shaved ice. A major supermarket (PX Mart) and local convenience stores are also a short walk away, making it easy to stock up for late-night drinks and snacks.
guide.faq_q1: Can we communicate in English or other languages?
guide.faq_a1: Yes! We offer support in English, Japanese, and Korean via our official LINE account or through Email (hellohouse2017@gmail.com). Feel free to contact us anytime.
guide.faq_q2: Can we store our luggage before check-in or after check-out?
guide.faq_a2: Yes, with prior notice, we can store your bags on the 1st floor common area, allowing you to explore the city luggage-free.
guide.faq_q3: What is the voltage and plug type in Taiwan?
guide.faq_a3: Taiwan uses a 110V voltage and Type A flat two-pin plug (same as Japan and USA). Most dual-voltage electronics can be plugged in directly.
guide.cta_sub: Create unforgettable memories with your loved ones. Hello House and Godin House are ready to welcome you.
